# Plan

**Data.** GEO GSE335287 (Liu et al. 2026, *Nat Cell Biol* 28:2321): ribo-seq and matched
RNA-seq of T3M4 pancreatic cancer cells, sgControl vs sgMETTL13. Raw gene-level counts,
keyed by gene symbol. Per the paper's methods, ribo counts are P-sites summed over RefSeq
CDSs.

**Replicates.** The deposited file has **2 replicates per condition**. The methods say three
biological replicates; only two are in GEO.

**Sign convention.** To match our MDA-MB-231 files (log2(sictrl / si3d), positive = factor
promotes), DESeq2 is run with **sgMETTL13 as reference and sgControl as test**:

> LFC = log2(sgControl / sgMETTL13). Positive = METTL13 promotes.

This is the **opposite** of Liu's own tables (sgMETTL13 / sgControl), which notebooks 01-03
used as-is.

**This first pass** loads the counts, keeps protein-coding genes, checks the knockdown and the
library PCA (Extended Data Fig. 5b), and plots count histograms to choose a count filter.
No filter and no DESeq2 yet.

# Load counts

```{r load}
counts_path <- here("accessories", "liu2026_GSE335287_raw_counts.txt")
raw <- read.delim(counts_path, check.names = FALSE)

stopifnot(names(raw)[1] == "geneID", ncol(raw) == 9,
          !anyDuplicated(raw$geneID), !anyNA(raw))

counts <- raw %>% column_to_rownames("geneID") %>% as.matrix()
stopifnot(all(counts >= 0), all(counts == round(counts)))

metadata <- tibble(sample_name = colnames(counts)) %>%
  separate(sample_name, c("condition", "library", "rep"), sep = "_", remove = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(library = tolower(library),
         comparison_variable = condition)

stopifnot(all(table(metadata$condition, metadata$library) == 2),
          setequal(metadata$condition, c("sgControl", "sgMETTL13")),
          setequal(metadata$library, c("ribo", "rna")))

knitr::kable(metadata)
cat("Genes:", nrow(counts), "\n")
```

# Keep protein-coding genes

The counts are summed over RefSeq CDSs, so nearly every gene is already protein-coding. Symbols
are matched to GENCODE v49; a gene is kept if any of its GENCODE entries has biotype
`protein_coding`. Genes with zero counts in all 8 libraries are dropped too.

```{r protein_coding}
anno <- read_tsv(here("accessories", "human", "gene_anno_hs_dm_v49_r111.tsv"),
                 col_names = c("gene_id", "symbol", "type", "species", "source"),
                 show_col_types = FALSE)
pc_symbols <- unique(anno$symbol[anno$type == "protein_coding"])

not_pc   <- setdiff(rownames(counts), pc_symbols)
all_zero <- rownames(counts)[rowSums(counts) == 0]

cat("Not protein-coding in GENCODE v49:", length(not_pc), "\n")
print(not_pc)
cat("Zero in all 8 libraries:", length(all_zero), "\n")

counts <- counts[!rownames(counts) %in% c(not_pc, all_zero), ]
stopifnot(all(rownames(counts) %in% pc_symbols), all(rowSums(counts) > 0),
          "METTL13" %in% rownames(counts))
cat("Genes kept:", nrow(counts), "\n")
```

# Library sizes and detected genes

```{r libsize}
lib_summary <- metadata %>%
  mutate(reads_millions = colSums(counts)[sample_name] / 1e6,
         genes_detected = colSums(counts > 0)[sample_name])
knitr::kable(lib_summary %>% dplyr::select(sample_name, library, reads_millions, genes_detected),
             digits = 2)
```

# Check 1: METTL13 knockdown

The knockdown target must fall in sgMETTL13. With our sign convention that is a **positive**
log2(sgControl / sgMETTL13). The values here come from DESeq2 size-factor-normalized counts,
with size factors estimated within each library type, before any model is fit. For
reference, Liu's separate RNA-seq (Supplementary Table 3, GSE292825) gives METTL13
log2(KD / WT) = -2.78, i.e. +2.78 in our convention. That is a different experiment, so
only the direction is asserted.

```{r check_knockdown}
norm_within <- function(lib) {
  m <- counts[, metadata$sample_name[metadata$library == lib]]
  sweep(m, 2, estimateSizeFactorsForMatrix(m), "/")
}
norm_counts <- cbind(norm_within("ribo"), norm_within("rna"))[, metadata$sample_name]

mettl13 <- metadata %>%
  mutate(norm_count = norm_counts["METTL13", sample_name]) %>%
  group_by(library) %>%
  summarise(sgControl = mean(norm_count[condition == "sgControl"]),
            sgMETTL13 = mean(norm_count[condition == "sgMETTL13"]),
            log2_sgControl_over_sgMETTL13 = log2(sgControl / sgMETTL13))
knitr::kable(mettl13, digits = 2)

stopifnot("METTL13 is not lower in sgMETTL13" =
            all(mettl13$log2_sgControl_over_sgMETTL13 > 1))
```

# Check 2: PCA of all libraries (Extended Data Fig. 5b)

The paper: libraries *"separate primarily by RNA source along PC1, while sgControl and
sgMETTL13 samples also segregate, particularly in the ribosome profiling data"*. VST on all 8
libraries with a blind design, using the 500 most variable genes (the `plotPCA` default).

```{r check_pca, fig.width = 5.5, fig.height = 4}
dds_all <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(counts, colData = as.data.frame(metadata), design = ~ 1)
vsd <- vst(dds_all, blind = TRUE)

pca_df <- plotPCA(vsd, intgroup = c("condition", "library"), returnData = TRUE)
pct    <- round(100 * attr(pca_df, "percentVar"), 1)

# PC1 must split ribo from RNA completely
pc1_by_lib <- split(pca_df$PC1, pca_df$library)
stopifnot("PC1 does not separate ribo from RNA" =
            max(pc1_by_lib$ribo) < min(pc1_by_lib$rna) ||
            min(pc1_by_lib$ribo) > max(pc1_by_lib$rna))

# Within ribo libraries, the two conditions must not overlap on PC2
ribo_pc2 <- pca_df %>% filter(library == "ribo") %>% { split(.$PC2, .$condition) }
cat("Ribo PC2 by condition:\n"); print(ribo_pc2)
stopifnot("PC2 does not separate conditions within ribo" =
            max(ribo_pc2$sgControl) < min(ribo_pc2$sgMETTL13) ||
            min(ribo_pc2$sgControl) > max(ribo_pc2$sgMETTL13))

condition_colors <- c(sgControl = "grey40", sgMETTL13 = "#0072B2")

p_pca <- ggplot(pca_df, aes(PC1, PC2, colour = condition, shape = library)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = condition_colors, name = NULL) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(ribo = 16, rna = 17), labels = c(ribo = "Ribo-seq", rna = "RNA-seq"),
                     name = NULL) +
  labs(x = sprintf("PC1 (%s%%)", pct[1]), y = sprintf("PC2 (%s%%)", pct[2]),
       title = "Liu 2026 T3M4 libraries",
       subtitle = sprintf("VST, top 500 variable genes; n = %d genes, 2 reps per group",
                          nrow(counts))) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12)
p_pca

if (isTRUE(params$save_plots))
  ggsave(here("plots", "liu2026_05_library_pca.pdf"), p_pca, width = 5.5, height = 4)
```

# Count histograms

One panel per library, log2(raw count + 1). Genes with a count of zero sit in the bar at 0. A
separate low-count hump would argue for a filter placed in the valley between the humps.

```{r histograms, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 4.5}
hist_df <- as_tibble(counts, rownames = "symbol") %>%
  pivot_longer(-symbol, names_to = "sample_name", values_to = "count") %>%
  left_join(metadata, by = "sample_name") %>%
  mutate(library = factor(library, levels = c("ribo", "rna"), labels = c("Ribo-seq", "RNA-seq")))

p_hist <- ggplot(hist_df, aes(log2(count + 1), fill = condition)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.25, boundary = 0) +
  facet_wrap(~ library + sample_name, nrow = 2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = condition_colors, guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "log2(raw count + 1)", y = "Genes",
       title = "Gene count distributions, Liu 2026 T3M4",
       subtitle = sprintf("n = %d protein-coding genes per library", nrow(counts))) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(strip.background = element_blank())
p_hist

if (isTRUE(params$save_plots))
  ggsave(here("plots", "liu2026_05_count_histograms.pdf"), p_hist, width = 9, height = 4.5)
```

## Summed counts per library type

As in `timecourse_qc.Rmd`: sum each gene's counts across the 4 RNA libraries and across the
4 ribo libraries, and plot log2(rowSums). The expression threshold is read off these
two histograms, applied to each library type separately, and a gene is kept only if it
passes in both.

```{r histogram_rowsums, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 3.5}
cts_rna  <- counts[, metadata$sample_name[metadata$library == "rna"]]
cts_ribo <- counts[, metadata$sample_name[metadata$library == "ribo"]]

cat("Genes with zero summed counts (not shown, log2 = -Inf): RNA", sum(rowSums(cts_rna) == 0),
    "| Ribo", sum(rowSums(cts_ribo) == 0), "\n")

par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
hist(log2(rowSums(cts_rna)),  breaks = 60, main = "RNA: log2(rowSums) distribution",
     xlab = "log2(summed count, 4 libraries)")
hist(log2(rowSums(cts_ribo)), breaks = 60, main = "Ribo: log2(rowSums) distribution",
     xlab = "log2(summed count, 4 libraries)")

if (isTRUE(params$save_plots)) {
  pdf(here("plots", "liu2026_05_rowsums_histograms.pdf"), width = 9, height = 3.5)
  par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
  hist(log2(rowSums(cts_rna)),  breaks = 60, main = "RNA: log2(rowSums) distribution",
       xlab = "log2(summed count, 4 libraries)")
  hist(log2(rowSums(cts_ribo)), breaks = 60, main = "Ribo: log2(rowSums) distribution",
       xlab = "log2(summed count, 4 libraries)")
  dev.off()
}
```

# Expression filter

Thresholds chosen from the histograms above: log2(rowSums) **> 8 in RNA** (> 256 reads over
4 libraries) and **> 6 in ribo** (> 64 reads). The ribo cut is lower because the ribo
libraries are about 4x shallower. A gene must pass both.

```{r filter}
rna_cut  <- 8
ribo_cut <- 6

keep_rna  <- rownames(cts_rna)[log2(rowSums(cts_rna))   > rna_cut]
keep_ribo <- rownames(cts_ribo)[log2(rowSums(cts_ribo)) > ribo_cut]
keep      <- intersect(keep_rna, keep_ribo)

cat("Pass RNA:", length(keep_rna), "| Pass Ribo:", length(keep_ribo), "| Pass both:", length(keep), "\n")

counts_filt <- counts[keep, ]
stopifnot("METTL13" %in% rownames(counts_filt))
```

# DESeq2

Same calls as `eif3e_eif3d_normoxia_and_hypoxia.Rmd`, without spike-ins (none were
sequenced), so size factors are standard median-of-ratios. **sgMETTL13 is the reference**,
so every LFC is log2(sgControl / sgMETTL13): positive = METTL13 promotes.

```{r deseq}
source(here("code", "functions.R"))

norm_matrix <- createNormMatrix(counts_filt, metadata, control_condition = "sgMETTL13")

run_mode <- function(mode) {
  deFunction(countsMatrix = counts_filt, allCounts_Norm = norm_matrix, metadata = metadata,
             control_condition = "sgMETTL13", test_condition = "sgControl", mode = mode)
}
res_rna  <- run_mode("RNA")
res_ribo <- run_mode("RIBO")
res_te   <- run_mode("TE")

results <- categorize_translation_changes(res_rna, res_ribo, res_te,
                                          padj_cutoff = 0.05, lfc_cutoff = 0)
knitr::kable(results$summary_table)
```

# Check 1 (DESeq2): METTL13 knockdown

```{r check_knockdown_deseq}
mettl13_res <- results$categorized_table %>% filter(gene_id == "METTL13")
knitr::kable(mettl13_res, digits = 3)

stopifnot("METTL13 rna_lfc should be strongly positive (sgControl / sgMETTL13)" =
            mettl13_res$rna_lfc > 1,
          "METTL13 ribo_lfc should be strongly positive (sgControl / sgMETTL13)" =
            mettl13_res$ribo_lfc > 1)

# Range checks
stopifnot(all(is.finite(c(res_rna$log2FoldChange, res_ribo$log2FoldChange, res_te$log2FoldChange))),
          all(c(res_rna$padj, res_ribo$padj, res_te$padj) >= 0 &
              c(res_rna$padj, res_ribo$padj, res_te$padj) <= 1, na.rm = TRUE))
```

# Volcano plots

Shrunken (apeglm) LFCs, as saved, against DESeq2 padj. Significant = padj < 0.05.
Positive LFC = lower in sgMETTL13 = METTL13 promotes.

```{r volcano, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 4}
volcano_df <- bind_rows(RNA = res_rna, Ribo = res_ribo, TE = res_te, .id = "readout") %>%
  dplyr::select(readout, gene_id, log2FoldChange, padj) %>%
  filter(!is.na(padj)) %>%
  mutate(readout = factor(readout, levels = c("RNA", "Ribo", "TE")),
         direction = case_when(padj < 0.05 & log2FoldChange > 0 ~ "METTL13 promotes",
                               padj < 0.05 & log2FoldChange < 0 ~ "METTL13 inhibits",
                               TRUE                             ~ "Not significant"),
         direction = factor(direction, levels = c("METTL13 promotes", "METTL13 inhibits",
                                                  "Not significant"))) %>%
  arrange(desc(direction))

volcano_n <- volcano_df %>%
  group_by(readout) %>%
  summarise(label = sprintf("promotes %d\ninhibits %d\nn = %d",
                            sum(direction == "METTL13 promotes"),
                            sum(direction == "METTL13 inhibits"), n()))

p_volcano <- ggplot(volcano_df, aes(log2FoldChange, -log10(padj), colour = direction)) +
  geom_point(size = 1, alpha = 0.7, stroke = 0) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(0.05), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
  geom_text(data = volcano_n, aes(x = Inf, y = Inf, label = label), inherit.aes = FALSE,
            hjust = 1.1, vjust = 1.2, size = 3) +
  facet_wrap(~ readout, nrow = 1) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("METTL13 promotes" = "#CC79A7", "METTL13 inhibits" = "#0072B2",
                                 "Not significant" = "grey70"), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "log2(sgControl / sgMETTL13), shrunken", y = "-log10 padj",
       title = "Liu 2026 T3M4, sgControl vs sgMETTL13",
       subtitle = "Positive = METTL13 promotes; DESeq2, 2 reps per group") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(strip.background = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom") +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 3, alpha = 1)))
p_volcano

if (isTRUE(params$save_plots))
  ggsave(here("plots", "liu2026_05_volcano_rna_ribo_te.pdf"), p_volcano, width = 10, height = 4)
```

# RNA, ribo and TE distributions with and without METTL13

Per gene and condition, from `createNormMatrix` (all 8 libraries normalized together):

- RNA = log2(mean normalized RNA count)
- Ribo = log2(mean normalized ribo count)
- TE = log2(mean normalized ribo / mean normalized RNA). The absolute TE offset is arbitrary
  but shared by both conditions.

Top row: each condition's distribution. Bottom row: the per-gene change, log2(sgControl /
sgMETTL13), **unshrunken**, because apeglm sets the DESeq2 RNA and TE LFCs to ~0 for almost
every gene (see the volcano).

```{r distributions, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 7}
mean_norm <- function(cond, lib)
  rowMeans(norm_matrix[, metadata$sample_name[metadata$condition == cond & metadata$library == lib]])

level_df <- bind_rows(
  RNA  = tibble(gene_id = rownames(norm_matrix),
                sgControl = log2(mean_norm("sgControl", "rna")),
                sgMETTL13 = log2(mean_norm("sgMETTL13", "rna"))),
  Ribo = tibble(gene_id = rownames(norm_matrix),
                sgControl = log2(mean_norm("sgControl", "ribo")),
                sgMETTL13 = log2(mean_norm("sgMETTL13", "ribo"))),
  TE   = tibble(gene_id = rownames(norm_matrix),
                sgControl = log2(mean_norm("sgControl", "ribo") / mean_norm("sgControl", "rna")),
                sgMETTL13 = log2(mean_norm("sgMETTL13", "ribo") / mean_norm("sgMETTL13", "rna"))),
  .id = "readout") %>%
  mutate(readout = factor(readout, levels = c("RNA", "Ribo", "TE")),
         change  = sgControl - sgMETTL13)
stopifnot(all(is.finite(level_df$sgControl)), all(is.finite(level_df$sgMETTL13)))

level_stats <- level_df %>%
  group_by(readout) %>%
  summarise(label_level = sprintf("median %.2f vs %.2f\npaired Wilcoxon p = %.2g\nn = %d genes",
                                  median(sgControl), median(sgMETTL13),
                                  wilcox.test(sgControl, sgMETTL13, paired = TRUE)$p.value, n()),
            label_change = sprintf("median %.3f\nn = %d genes", median(change), n()))
knitr::kable(level_stats)

level_long <- level_df %>%
  pivot_longer(c(sgControl, sgMETTL13), names_to = "condition", values_to = "value")

p_level <- ggplot(level_long, aes(value, colour = condition, fill = condition)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.15, linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_text(data = level_stats, aes(x = Inf, y = Inf, label = label_level), inherit.aes = FALSE,
            hjust = 1.05, vjust = 1.2, size = 3) +
  facet_wrap(~ readout, nrow = 1, scales = "free") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = condition_colors, name = NULL) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = condition_colors, name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "log2 normalized count (RNA, Ribo) or log2(ribo / RNA) (TE)", y = "Density",
       title = "Per condition") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(strip.background = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom")

p_change <- ggplot(level_df, aes(change)) +
  geom_density(colour = "black", fill = "black", alpha = 0.15, linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
  geom_text(data = level_stats, aes(x = Inf, y = Inf, label = label_change), inherit.aes = FALSE,
            hjust = 1.05, vjust = 1.2, size = 3) +
  facet_wrap(~ readout, nrow = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "log2(sgControl / sgMETTL13), unshrunken", y = "Density",
       title = "Change", subtitle = "Positive = METTL13 promotes") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(strip.background = element_blank())

p_dist <- patchwork::wrap_plots(p_level, p_change, ncol = 1)
p_dist

if (isTRUE(params$save_plots))
  ggsave(here("plots", "liu2026_05_rna_ribo_te_distributions.pdf"), p_dist, width = 11, height = 7)
```

# Replicate concordance

The RNA arm returns no significant genes, not even METTL13. Spearman correlation of
normalized log2 counts within each library type, on the filtered genes, shows why.

```{r replicate_cor}
norm_filt <- log2(norm_matrix + 1)
for (lib in c("ribo", "rna")) {
  s <- metadata$sample_name[metadata$library == lib]
  cat("\n", lib, "\n")
  print(round(cor(norm_filt[, s], method = "spearman"), 3))
}

dispersion_floor <- function(lib) {
  s   <- metadata$sample_name[metadata$library == lib]
  cd  <- data.frame(Condition = factor(metadata$condition[match(s, metadata$sample_name)]))
  dds <- DESeq(DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(counts_filt[, s], cd, ~ Condition), quiet = TRUE)
  median(dispersions(dds))
}
disp <- c(ribo = dispersion_floor("ribo"), rna = dispersion_floor("rna"))
knitr::kable(tibble(library = names(disp), median_dispersion = disp,
                    implied_cv = sqrt(disp)), digits = 3)
```

**Do the RNA changes replicate?** Compute the log2(sgControl / sgMETTL13) change twice, once
from the rep1 libraries and once from rep2, and correlate the two across genes. A real change
gives a positive correlation.

```{r replicate_lfc}
rep_change <- function(lib, rep) {
  ctl <- metadata$sample_name[metadata$library == lib & metadata$condition == "sgControl" & metadata$rep == rep]
  ko  <- metadata$sample_name[metadata$library == lib & metadata$condition == "sgMETTL13" & metadata$rep == rep]
  log2((norm_matrix[, ctl] + 1) / (norm_matrix[, ko] + 1))
}
rep_cor <- sapply(c(ribo = "ribo", rna = "rna"), function(lib)
  cor(rep_change(lib, "rep1"), rep_change(lib, "rep2"), method = "spearman"))
knitr::kable(tibble(library = names(rep_cor), rep1_vs_rep2_change_spearman = rep_cor), digits = 3)

stopifnot("ribo changes should replicate" = rep_cor[["ribo"]] > 0.4)

# Cross-paired check: rep1 control with rep2 KO, vs rep2 control with rep1 KO. If the RNA
# anticorrelation is about specific libraries rather than how replicates were paired, it
# should survive re-pairing.
cross_change <- function(lib, ctl_rep, ko_rep) {
  ctl <- metadata$sample_name[metadata$library == lib & metadata$condition == "sgControl" & metadata$rep == ctl_rep]
  ko  <- metadata$sample_name[metadata$library == lib & metadata$condition == "sgMETTL13" & metadata$rep == ko_rep]
  log2((norm_matrix[, ctl] + 1) / (norm_matrix[, ko] + 1))
}
cross_cor <- sapply(c(ribo = "ribo", rna = "rna"), function(lib)
  cor(cross_change(lib, "rep1", "rep2"), cross_change(lib, "rep2", "rep1"), method = "spearman"))
knitr::kable(tibble(library = names(cross_cor), cross_paired_change_spearman = cross_cor), digits = 3)
```

## Heatmaps

Left: Spearman correlation of all 8 libraries (log2 normalized counts). Every pair is
positive, so the RNA problem shows only as `sgMETTL13_RNA_rep1` being the palest row. Right:
Spearman correlation of the four replicate-level changes, log2(sgControl / sgMETTL13). This is
where the anticorrelation is visible.

```{r heatmaps, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 5}
sample_cor <- cor(norm_filt, method = "spearman")
annot <- metadata %>% dplyr::select(sample_name, condition, library) %>%
  column_to_rownames("sample_name") %>% as.data.frame()
annot_colors <- list(condition = condition_colors,
                     library = c(ribo = "grey20", rna = "grey85"))

pheatmap::pheatmap(sample_cor, display_numbers = TRUE, number_format = "%.3f",
                   annotation_row = annot, annotation_col = annot, annotation_colors = annot_colors,
                   color = colorRampPalette(c("white", "#D55E00"))(100),
                   main = sprintf("Library correlation, Spearman (n = %d genes)", nrow(norm_filt)))
if (isTRUE(params$save_plots))
  pheatmap::pheatmap(sample_cor, display_numbers = TRUE, number_format = "%.3f",
                     annotation_row = annot, annotation_col = annot, annotation_colors = annot_colors,
                     color = colorRampPalette(c("white", "#D55E00"))(100),
                     main = sprintf("Library correlation, Spearman (n = %d genes)", nrow(norm_filt)),
                     filename = here("plots", "liu2026_05_heatmap_library_correlation.pdf"),
                     width = 7, height = 6)
```

RNA and ribo libraries separately, each on its own color scale so that the within-type
differences are visible (in the combined heatmap they are compressed by the ribo-vs-RNA gap).

```{r heatmaps_by_library, fig.width = 5.5, fig.height = 4.2}
library_heatmap <- function(lib, filename = NA) {
  s <- metadata$sample_name[metadata$library == lib]
  m <- sample_cor[s, s]
  pheatmap::pheatmap(m, display_numbers = TRUE, number_format = "%.3f",
                     annotation_row = annot[s, "condition", drop = FALSE],
                     annotation_col = annot[s, "condition", drop = FALSE],
                     annotation_colors = list(condition = condition_colors),
                     color = colorRampPalette(c("white", "#D55E00"))(100),
                     breaks = seq(min(m), 1, length.out = 101),
                     main = sprintf("%s libraries\nSpearman, n = %d genes",
                                    c(ribo = "Ribo-seq", rna = "RNA-seq")[[lib]], nrow(norm_filt)),
                     filename = filename, width = 5.5, height = 4.2)
}
for (lib in c("rna", "ribo")) {
  library_heatmap(lib)
  if (isTRUE(params$save_plots))
    library_heatmap(lib, here("plots", sprintf("liu2026_05_heatmap_%s_library_correlation.pdf", lib)))
}
```

```{r heatmap_changes, fig.width = 5, fig.height = 4.2}
change_mat <- cbind(`RNA rep1`  = rep_change("rna",  "rep1"), `RNA rep2`  = rep_change("rna",  "rep2"),
                    `Ribo rep1` = rep_change("ribo", "rep1"), `Ribo rep2` = rep_change("ribo", "rep2"))
change_cor <- cor(change_mat, method = "spearman")
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(change_cor["RNA rep1", "RNA rep2"], rep_cor[["rna"]])))

change_heatmap <- function(filename = NA)
  pheatmap::pheatmap(change_cor, display_numbers = TRUE, number_format = "%.2f",
                     cluster_rows = FALSE, cluster_cols = FALSE,
                     color = colorRampPalette(c("#0072B2", "white", "#D55E00"))(100),
                     breaks = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 101),
                     main = sprintf("Change log2(sgControl / sgMETTL13)\nper replicate, Spearman (n = %d genes)",
                                    nrow(change_mat)),
                     filename = filename, width = 5, height = 4.2)
change_heatmap()
if (isTRUE(params$save_plots))
  change_heatmap(here("plots", "liu2026_05_heatmap_replicate_change_correlation.pdf"))
```

**Finding.** The ribo change replicates (Spearman ~+0.63). The RNA change does **not**: the
rep1 and rep2 estimates are *anti*-correlated (~-0.38), and re-pairing the replicates makes it
stronger (~-0.74), so it comes from the libraries, not from how they were paired. It traces
mainly to `sgMETTL13_RNA_rep1`, which correlates worse with its own replicate than with either
control and is the RNA library most similar to the ribo libraries (library heatmap below). So this dataset cannot
say whether mRNA levels change on METTL13 loss, and that noise passes straight into TE, because
TE is ribo relative to RNA. In practice:

- **Ribo LFC is the reliable readout** from this dataset (1,366 genes at padj < 0.05).
- **RNA LFC is uninformative** (0 genes significant; apeglm shrinks all to ~0).
- **TE LFC** is usable only unshrunken, as a noisy ranking; shrunken, only ~5 genes are
  confidently non-zero (apeglm s-value < 0.01, next section).

For RNA-level questions, use Liu's separate RNA-seq (Supplementary Table 3, GSE292825).

# Unshrunken LFCs and s-values

`deFunction()` returns only apeglm-shrunken LFCs. The same three models are refit here to keep
the unshrunken (MLE) LFCs and apeglm **s-values** (the probability that the sign of the shrunken
LFC is wrong; the confidence measure that matches a shrunken estimate). The refit must reproduce
`deFunction`'s shrunken LFCs, which proves it is the same model.

```{r mle_svalue}
fit_mode <- function(mode) {
  s  <- if (mode == "TE") metadata$sample_name else
        metadata$sample_name[metadata$library == tolower(mode)]
  cd <- metadata %>% filter(sample_name %in% s) %>%
    mutate(Condition = factor(condition, levels = c("sgMETTL13", "sgControl")),
           SeqType   = factor(library, levels = c("rna", "ribo"))) %>%
    as.data.frame()
  design <- if (mode == "TE") ~ Condition + SeqType + Condition:SeqType else ~ Condition
  coef   <- if (mode == "TE") "ConditionsgControl.SeqTyperibo" else "Condition_sgControl_vs_sgMETTL13"
  dds <- DESeq(DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(counts_filt[, cd$sample_name], cd, design), quiet = TRUE)
  mle <- results(dds, name = coef, independentFiltering = FALSE)
  shr <- lfcShrink(dds, coef = coef, type = "apeglm", svalue = TRUE, quiet = TRUE)
  tibble(gene_id = rownames(mle), lfc_mle = mle$log2FoldChange,
         lfc_shrunk = shr$log2FoldChange, svalue = shr$svalue)
}
refit <- map(c(rna = "RNA", ribo = "RIBO", te = "TE"), fit_mode)

# Same model as deFunction: shrunken LFCs must agree
for (m in names(refit)) {
  ref <- list(rna = res_rna, ribo = res_ribo, te = res_te)[[m]]
  d <- max(abs(refit[[m]]$lfc_shrunk - ref$log2FoldChange[match(refit[[m]]$gene_id, ref$gene_id)]))
  cat(m, "max |refit - deFunction| shrunken LFC:", signif(d, 2), "\n")
  stopifnot("refit does not reproduce deFunction" = d < 1e-3)
}

refit_wide <- imap(refit, ~ .x %>% dplyr::select(gene_id, lfc_mle, svalue) %>%
                     rename_with(function(n) paste0(.y, "_", n), -gene_id)) %>%
  purrr::reduce(left_join, by = "gene_id")

tibble(readout = names(refit),
       `s < 0.005` = map_int(refit, ~ sum(.x$svalue < 0.005)),
       `s < 0.01`  = map_int(refit, ~ sum(.x$svalue < 0.01)),
       `s < 0.05`  = map_int(refit, ~ sum(.x$svalue < 0.05))) %>% knitr::kable()

cat("TE genes with s-value < 0.01:\n")
refit$te %>% filter(svalue < 0.01) %>% arrange(svalue) %>% knitr::kable(digits = 4)
```

# Save

Same columns as our `translation_categories_*.csv` files (`*_lfc` are apeglm-shrunken), plus
`{rna,ribo,te}_lfc_mle` (unshrunken) and `{rna,ribo,te}_svalue`. `gene_id` holds the **gene
symbol** here, because the GEO counts carry no Ensembl IDs; `symbol` repeats it so joins on
`symbol` work as they do on our files.

```{r save}
out <- results$categorized_table %>%
  left_join(res_rna  %>% dplyr::select(gene_id, rna_padj  = padj), by = "gene_id") %>%
  left_join(res_ribo %>% dplyr::select(gene_id, ribo_padj = padj), by = "gene_id") %>%
  left_join(res_te   %>% dplyr::select(gene_id, te_padj   = padj), by = "gene_id") %>%
  left_join(refit_wide, by = "gene_id") %>%
  mutate(symbol = gene_id)
stopifnot(all(is.finite(out$te_lfc_mle)), all(is.finite(out$ribo_lfc_mle)))

stopifnot(nrow(out) == nrow(counts_filt), !anyDuplicated(out$gene_id))

out_dir <- here("output", "translational_control_overview", "liu2026_eef1a_k55me2")
dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
write_csv(out, file.path(out_dir, "translation_categories_sgcontrol_vs_sgmettl13_liu2026.csv"))
write_csv(results$summary_table,
          file.path(out_dir, "translation_summary_sgcontrol_vs_sgmettl13_liu2026.csv"))
cat("Wrote", nrow(out), "genes\n")
```
